newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament adopts takeover law.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament adopts takeover law.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament said on Wednesday it had passed a merger law giving the state watchdog control over all purchases amounting to over 25 percent of a company.

According to the law the Securities Market Agency will manage the purchase of over 25 percent of shares of a company that is listed on the Ljubljana bourse or that has equity capital of at least one billion tolars ($6.3 million).
The same will apply to smaller companies with over 500 shareholders.
In the case of newly-privatised companies, the government must approve any purchase of over 25 percent of shares of firms whose equity capital exceeds 800 million tolars ($5.1 million).
The law is expected to be enforced at the end of July, providing it is passed by the State Council, the Upper House of parliament, which has a right to veto it by Wednesday.
Until now Slovenia has had no legislation on takeovers. ($ = 158 Slovenian Tolars)
